purpose: Test whether training under variable robot-ground impact response makes one high-speed drift policy transfer from nominal Isaac to the nominal MuJoCo model.
status_at_creation: full_training_running; final policy and paired verdict unknown
training_material: 32 sampled robot restitution buckets at startup; ground restitution remains 0.0; friction remains 0.15 in both engines
deterministic_evaluation_material: Robot and ground restitution both 0.0 in Isaac; nominal unmodified audited MJCF in MuJoCo

training.motor_domain_profile: motor-v1; unchanged torque, speed and axle-friction ranges
training.checkpoint_selection: final model only, no intermediate checkpoint selection

success_requires: Same exported final normalized actor in deterministic nominal Isaac and nominal MuJoCo, both full clips and both PASS under unchanged native-200-Hz assess_drift_turn.py gate. No gap bridging, no soft-contact substitution, no post-hoc speed relaxation.
limitations: One candidate and one deterministic evaluation seed cannot establish robustness.
Restitution randomization is a robustness intervention, not a calibrated equivalence between PhysX and MuJoCo contact solvers.
